laws.rule: In Krka National Park, swimming at Skradinski buk waterfall is not allowed, and dogs must be on a lead throughout the park. The park's FAQ lists Roški slap, Stinice and Pisak as the only places swimming is allowed, from 1 June to 30 September.
laws.heading: Javna ustanova Nacionalni park Krka

laws.rule: Kornati National Park: visitors are not allowed in its four strict-protection zones, including the waters around Purara, Mrtenjak, Kolobučar and the Obručan islets.
Kornati National Park: anchoring and staying overnight are allowed only in the bays and coves named in the park rules. Check the current park map and boating conditions before entry.

layers.process: Kornati National Park is entered by boat and the ticket is per vessel, set by vessel length and season. For 2026 a vessel up to 6.99 m pays EUR 25 for one day from October to May and EUR 45 from June to September when the ticket is bought outside the park (about A$39.73 and A$71.51 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293); bought inside the park the same vessel pays EUR 45 and EUR 90. Larger vessels pay more (an 11 to 17.99 m vessel pays EUR 50 or 95 bought outside). Vessels without a motor pay EUR 7 per person per day. Three-day and five-day tickets exist, and a joint Kornati and Telašćica ticket is sold only on the mySea portal.

The Kornati price list charges for filming: commercial filming or photography EUR 800 a day (EUR 1,600 for 7 days), and drone filming, where the needed permits are obtained, EUR 1,400 a day (about A$1,271, A$2,543 and A$2,225 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026).
